newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan PM Treasuries comment wrongly reported -- MOF.
newsitem.headline: Japan PM Treasuries comment wrongly reported -- MOF.

text.p: Comments by Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto on Japanese investments in U.S. Treasuries were incorrectly reported, Finance Minister Hiroshi Mitsuzuka told reporters on Tuesday.
"The prime minister's real intention was not reported correctly," he said.
A senior MOF official told reporters that U.S. Treasuries are an essential investment tool in Japan's foreign reserves.
"U.S. Treasuries are a highly advantageous, secure and essential investment instrument for Japan's foreign currency reserves," the official said.

The official also said the Japanese Finance Ministry and the U.S. Treasury Department were on very good terms and that he highly evaluated the performance of Treasury Secretary Robert Rubin and Deputy Treasury Secretary Lawrence Summers.
Comments by Hashimoto in New York on Monday about potential sales of U.S. Treasuries by Japan caused turmoil in U.S. financial markets late on Monday.

Hashimoto, responding to a question after a speech at Columbia University, said Japan had in the past been tempted to sell its holdings of U.S. Treasury securities and boost its gold reserves, but had not done so.

"I hope the U.S. will engage in efforts and in cooperation to maintain exchange stability so we will not succumb to the temptation to sell off Treasury bills and switch our funds to gold," Hashimoto added.
